searchText: sounds about right the first deployment of sharding will not have any execution -- so users of the shards will just post a sequence of bytes when they need to post data to some shard validators in the system propose shard blocks and other validators confirm those shard blocks are available if i know some data is available then i can do things like e.g. build a rollup on top of it so yeah you can imagine arbitrum, optimism, etc. will post L2 blocks as shard blobs which are confirmed by the L1 validators these L2 sequencers will follow the L1 consensus to know what has been confirmed (i.e. letting them compute the latest L2 state) details of the networking are still to be determined but any user of a shard should be able to get any data onto any particular shard and it won't really matter as long as that user can track which blobs are where e.g. arbitrum posts to shards 1, 2, 7, optimism posts to shards 4, 5, 6, dydx posts to shard 2 but just in a different part of the shard chain than arbitrum (note: users can even share a given shard block, they don't need to be in distinct shard blocks) there is no higher-level structure like a "transaction hash" or a "addresses" so you don't need to worry about sharding on those "keys" and bc there is no execution we don't have to worry about the complexities of cross-shard execution (kind of the point to go for data sharding before execution sharding) so its better to think about the shards as just a uniform data layer that applications can use for availability there will be details/mechanics to resolve like which data gets into which shard at which block but at this point it is more just like "punctuation" that a user of the shards doesn't really need to worry about
